callerEquivalence.successfulStdout: Unchanged UTF-8 stdout, including JSON consumed by all three existing callers; tested with Korean and multibyte characters.
callerEquivalence.sshPolicy: BatchMode=yes, StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, HostKeyAlias, ConnectTimeout=10, target port/user/address and python3 stdin preserved; exact argv tested.
callerEquivalence.backendJobs: Native background prepare/deploy jobTimeoutMs remains unchanged, including the admitted six-hour policy. Foreground calls receive 120000 ms; multi-step owner handoff receives 600000 ms; backend stdout cap is 16 MiB.
callerEquivalence.observationAndLifecycle: 180000 ms foreground budget covers sequential native probes and stop/DOWN/lock/start steps; default stdout cap 8 MiB and stderr cap 64 KiB.
callerEquivalence.failureSemantics: No raw stderr or failure stdout is persisted. Structured stage/reason, observed byte counts, child creation, actual exit/signal, reap and bounded cleanup observations are retained. Timeout/output caps do not establish remote cancellation.
callerEquivalence.requestFences: Nonzero or malformed native results become uncertain; same-request invocation refuses replay. Failed receipt/result persistence retains the local request lock; completed results remain replayed as records, without rerunning native execution.

verification.install: bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --backend=copyfile; isolated worktree only; lockfile unchanged

newCases: Exact SSH arguments, successful UTF-8/JSON stdout and sanitized stderr
Nonzero exit with raw failure output omitted
Deadline with SIGTERM-resistant inert child and SIGKILL reap
Durable launch-pending uncertainty before spawn and sanitized spawn rejection
Deadline after direct child exit while pipes remain open
Unconfirmed cleanup stays bounded; late exit cannot rewrite settled receipt
Invalid budgets reject before spawn and explicit longer budget preserves success
Uncertain lifecycle failure and malformed-success result both block second execution
Receipt persistence rejection retains request lock and blocks second execution

residualLimits: Real remote/runtime qualification and native serving were not executed; independent exact-tree review and current native gates remain required.
Unexpectedly slow or verbose foreground output now fails conservatively under explicit budgets; remote effects remain uncertain and never admit automatic replay.
Only the directly owned SSH transport is signalled. A failed reap or pipe cancellation stays explicitly unconfirmed; no descendant or remote-process termination is inferred.
Successful native JSON stdout remains the existing caller-owned payload; this change sanitizes transport diagnostics and failure output rather than rewriting native response contracts.
